caption: We lost R16 000 a month overnight and we're still here. What would you have cut first?

slides.title:
How we spend
our R22 500
since his retrenchment
Living in Carletonville
slides.body:
Him 34, her 31
Married, two kids (9 and 6)
Jobs: General labourer, was a mine machine operator until March & till supervisor at a hardware store
Combined net: R22 500 p/m (down from R38 000)

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 3 bed flat, moved out of the house we bonded in April
slides.body: We sold the house before the bank could take it. Some weeks that still feels like the win.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Two kids, one of them a teenager who eats like three
slides.body: This is the number I watch most closely now. It used to be the one I never checked.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: The one car we kept, the other went back to the bank
slides.body: He needs it for piece jobs. We decided food would move before the car did.

slides.title: Transport & fuel
slides.includes: Petrol for piece jobs, taxi fare for her shifts
slides.body: Piece jobs pay per site. Some weeks the petrol costs more than the job did.

slides.title: Store account repayments
slides.includes: Furniture and back-to-school accounts from before March
slides.body: We opened these when there was still a mine salary. They didn't get the memo when it ended.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Electricity, water, medical aid, school fees, insurance, phone & data
slides.body: Same categories as before. Every single amount inside them got smaller this year.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R22 500. Sixteen thousand less than we used to have, and we still made rent.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
We uploaded our statements to Beyond Horizon the month he was retrenched, just to see where we actually stood.

No bank login needed.
